review_comments.body:
### Env token mixed with explicit keys **Medium Severity** `aws_session_token` falls back to `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` on its own, then is attached whenever static keys are present. Keys from `api_config` therefore inherit a leftover environment token, which boto3 would not mix in, so previously valid long-lived keys are sent as mismatched temporary credentials and Bedrock rejects them.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8317e628a83e0f55d9ff12c8b44704e146d96352. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

With `api_config={"aws_session_token": "token"}` and no environment keys, the constructor calls `boto3.client` with only `region_name`. That silently discards the explicit token and lets the dimension check run under whichever profile or role boto3 finds. Please reject an explicit token without its access key and secret before creating the client, and cover that case alongside the partial-key test.

Copying environment credentials into client arguments loses botocore’s refresh support. With an environment key pair, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` and `AWS_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRATION`, I verified that a plain boto3 client gets `RefreshableCredentials`, while this vectorizer gets fixed `Credentials`. A long-lived vectorizer will keep signing with the original credentials after they expire, even if the process updates its environment. Please let boto3 resolve environment credentials whenever the caller supplies no explicit credentials. The environment-token test should cover that behaviour without requiring RedisVL to copy the token into kwargs.

`client_kwargs.update(kwargs)` can replace one half of a credential pair after validation. With a complete pair in `api_config` and a different `aws_access_key_id` passed directly to the constructor, I observed boto3 receive the second ID with the first pair’s secret. Previously the duplicate keyword failed immediately. Please reject conflicting credential arguments before creating the client and keep forwarding unrelated boto3 options.

When the default chain finds no credentials, client creation succeeds and the constructor proceeds to the dimension check. With empty AWS config files and instance metadata disabled, I counted six embedding attempts. The final `ValueError` reported `Error setting embedding model dimensions: RetryError[...]`, hiding the missing-credentials diagnosis. Please preserve botocore’s `NoCredentialsError` through the embedding path and exclude it from retries. A caller with no configured credentials should get an actionable error on the first attempt.

### Partial credentials still retried **Medium Severity** `PartialCredentialsError` from boto3's default chain is converted to `ValueError` in `_embed` and `_embed_many`, so `_is_retryable` never sees it. Incomplete environment keys are retried up to six times and then hidden behind a wrapped `RetryError` from the dimension check. The reviewer brief's `NoCredentialsError` handling does not cover this sibling.
Additional Locations (2) - [`redisvl/utils/vectorize/bedrock.py#L340-L344`](https://github.com/redis/redis-vl-python/blob/70fffae4c5db37bf63714b5f4e829c6d542e7bca/redisvl/utils/vectorize/bedrock.py#L340-L344) - [`redisvl/utils/vectorize/bedrock.py#L24-L33`](https://github.com/redis/redis-vl-python/blob/70fffae4c5db37bf63714b5f4e829c6d542e7bca/redisvl/utils/vectorize/bedrock.py#L24-L33)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 70fffae4c5db37bf63714b5f4e829c6d542e7bca. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

An SSO profile with no cached login still retries six times and hides the reason. With a real boto3 SSO profile and an empty token cache, botocore raised `SSOTokenLoadError` before making any network request. `BedrockVectorizer()` caught that exception during the dimension check and ultimately raised `ValueError: Error setting embedding model dimensions: RetryError[...]`. Please preserve `SSOTokenLoadError` through the single and batch embedding paths and the constructor, and exclude it from retries. A regression test should assert that the first attempt surfaces the missing SSO login.

These two exception tests import `botocore` directly, although the Bedrock SDK is optional. With botocore imports disabled, the other eight tests passed and these two failed with `ModuleNotFoundError`. Please use `pytest.importorskip("botocore.exceptions")` in the SDK-dependent tests so contributors can run the rest without the Bedrock extra.

comments.body:
Pushed a follow-up commit (62ab031): `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` from the environment is now only used when the access key and secret also come from the environment. If explicit keys are passed in `api_config`, a leftover environment token is no longer attached to them (that mix would fail authentication). Added a unit test for this case.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks for the detailed review. Pushed a follow-up commit addressing all four points:

- Environment credentials (including `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`) are no longer copied into the client kwargs; when no explicit credentials are supplied, boto3 resolves them itself, so refreshable credentials keep working. The env-token test now asserts nothing is copied.
- An explicit `aws_session_token` without access key and secret now raises `ValueError` before the client is created.
- Conflicting credential values between `api_config` and constructor kwargs raise `ValueError`; unrelated boto3 kwargs are still forwarded.
- `NoCredentialsError` is excluded from the tenacity retries and propagates unwrapped from `_embed`, `_embed_many` and the dimension check, so a caller with no credentials gets it on the first attempt.

Unit tests cover each case.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
